source: AIHSR Risk Reference Tool v1.5 (Tamiko Eto)

prompts.text: The protocol reports the demographics of the training dataset and notes any known gaps or limitations
The protocol describes how potential bias in the dataset will be evaluated before model training
The protocol includes a plan for checking and reducing bias so that no group is unfairly treated
The protocol explains how the investigator will verify that the AI does not unfairly harm or exclude marginalized groups
The protocol describes safeguards to ensure participants will not be exposed to harmful, offensive, or distressing AI-generated content during the study
The protocol addresses what happens if participants are accidentally exposed to inappropriate or toxic material, including immediate protections (e.g., withdrawal, reporting, counseling referral)
The protocol describes how the model will be tested on new and diverse datasets beyond those used in training
The protocol describes the strategy for bias evaluation and fairness testing across subgroups (e.g., race, gender, age)
The protocol reports training data demographics and known limits of the dataset
The protocol includes subgroup analysis or fairness checks in the prediction study
The protocol describes a plan for ongoing monitoring of AI performance after deployment, including how performance drift, new biases, or unintended harms will be detected over time
The protocol describes a plan for ongoing fairness evaluations to ensure the tool continues to perform equitably across subgroups
The protocol describes how the investigator will ensure subgroups are not at greater risk (e.g., checking for bias in the dataset)
The protocol describes the de-identification process to reduce re-identification risk
The protocol describes how secondary data use complies with privacy requirements and participant consent limitations
The protocol addresses re-identification risk in AI prompts/embeddings and describes how this risk will be reduced
The protocol describes the de-identification or aggregation methods that will be used to protect identities
The protocol includes a plan to prevent the AI from exposing sensitive personal data
The protocol describes how patient privacy will be maintained during real-world use, including protections against re-identification or unintended inference
The protocol outlines how the dataset will be secured to prevent unauthorized access or breaches
The protocol describes how study data and AI system access will be protected against unauthorized use or cyberattacks, including who will be responsible for monitoring for breaches
The protocol addresses corrective steps if the AI system is compromised, including how to stop an attack, notify participants, and prevent harm
The protocol explains how the project ensures real-world relevance (e.g., that correlations found are linked to meaningful clinical associations, not just statistical patterns)
The protocol includes a plan for how harm will be prevented if the tool produces wrong or misleading results
The protocol describes a plan for documenting early limitations of the model and how those will be addressed before moving to validation
The protocol includes a plan for testing model performance on incomplete or messy records ('edge cases')
The protocol describes how the investigator will ensure the AI does not mislead participants or present biased/misinformation that could influence their decisions
The protocol describes how participant data will be used and ensures the system does not engage in hidden tracking, surveillance, or manipulation of vulnerable groups
The protocol describes safeguards in place to prevent the AI system from being misused in ways that could cause large-scale harm (e.g., altering medical devices, mass data leaks)
The protocol documents who is responsible for monitoring the AI system for misuse, and what steps will be taken if harmful use is detected

fraud-manipulation-4.3.shortName: Tool Involves Any Form of Deception

prompts.text: The protocol describes measures to prevent the AI system from generating deceptive or manipulative outputs that could affect participant decision-making
The protocol describes how participants will be informed, in plain language, about the risks of fraud or manipulation if interacting with the AI system
The protocol describes how the AI's performance will be compared against existing practice (e.g., standard-of-care approaches) and identifies those existing practices
The protocol describes a plan for human oversight, including who checks the AI output and how
The protocol outlines safeguards against automation bias (clinicians over-relying on AI without critical judgment)

loss-of-agency-5.2.shortName: Respect for Person (End-User or Participant Does Not Have Choice if AI is Used)

prompts.text: The protocol describes the authorization and consent process for gaining access to the data (e.g., IRB approval, consent, HIPAA authorization, data use agreements)
The protocol describes how consent for prospective validation participation will be obtained, including how participants are informed that AI is being tested
The protocol addresses re-consent procedures if the scope of AI use changes during the validation phase
The protocol describes how participants will be informed about the AI's role and how AI affects their care or data
The protocol describes how chatbot or AI system responses will be explained to users, including the intended use, limitations, potential hallucination, and guidance on appropriate engagement
The protocol describes the informed consent process for real-world AI use, including clear disclosure that AI contributes to clinical decisions
The protocol addresses ongoing consent for adaptive AI systems where model behavior may change over time
The protocol describes participants' right to contest or override AI-driven decisions affecting their care
The protocol includes a deception debriefing plan if participants were not initially informed of AI involvement
The protocol describes how human-in-the-loop oversight will be ensured for all AI-supported decisions that could affect patient safety or clinical outcomes
The protocol describes how risks and limitations of the AI tool will be communicated to participants, clinicians, and other stakeholders
The protocol describes how benefits of the AI system will be shared fairly across participant groups and not restricted to one group or institution
The protocol addresses steps to avoid concentrating control or decision-making power in one entity, to the detriment of research participants
The protocol addresses the risk that the AI may replace or reduce the role of teachers, clinicians, or staff, and describes how participant concerns about job loss will be mitigated
The protocol describes how the study will avoid worsening disparities in workforce opportunities, particularly for vulnerable or underrepresented groups
The protocol addresses concerns that the AI system may devalue human contributions (e.g., replacing teachers' feedback or clinicians' judgment) in this study
The protocol describes how participants will be informed that human oversight remains central, and how their input will be recognized and respected
The protocol addresses whether competitive or market pressures have influenced the development timeline, and confirms that safety requirements have not been compromised
The protocol describes how the investigator will ensure validation testing is not abbreviated or findings overlooked due to competitive dynamics
The protocol includes a commitment to transparent reporting of safety concerns regardless of potential market or competitive implications

governance-failure-6.5.shortName: Lacking Required Oversight or Failing to Adhere to Required Standards

prompts.text: The protocol describes how the study aligns with FDA or other regulatory expectations for validation
The protocol provides a governance plan for accountability, including who is responsible for oversight of AI outputs, and how adverse events or errors will be reported and acted upon
The protocol outlines the process for participant recourse if they believe they were harmed or excluded due to AI-driven decisions
The protocol describes how the study ensures compliance with FDA post-market surveillance (if classified as a device) or other applicable regulatory requirements
The protocol includes a plan for how errors will be handled so patients are not harmed or excluded
The protocol documents the computational resources required for model training and acknowledges associated energy consumption
The protocol describes efforts to minimize environmental impact during iterative model evaluation and hyperparameter tuning
The protocol addresses the expected environmental footprint of inference at deployment scale and any plans to mitigate ongoing energy consumption
The protocol describes how the objective function and training process are designed to align with intended human values and clinical goals
The protocol describes testing procedures to detect whether the model pursues objectives different from those intended, including in novel situations
The protocol includes monitoring to detect if the AI optimizes for metrics that conflict with patient welfare or games evaluation criteria during deployment
The protocol addresses whether the model may have acquired unintended harmful capabilities through its training data or process
The protocol describes red-teaming or specialized testing to identify latent dangerous capabilities not surfaced by standard testing
The protocol includes safeguards to prevent the model from being exploited to provide harmful information or assist malicious actors beyond the intended healthcare context
The protocol describes how the training data distribution represents real-world variability and addresses potential brittleness to distribution shift
The protocol describes testing that includes edge cases, out-of-distribution data, and stress conditions to reveal model failures
The protocol includes monitoring for unpredictable failures when the model encounters unusual patient presentations, data quality issues, or conditions differing from the training distribution
The protocol describes fallback procedures when the AI system fails or produces unreliable outputs during clinical use
The protocol describes how end-users (e.g., clinicians) will provide structured feedback on the AI's usefulness, clarity, and transparency when using/testing it
The protocol addresses how the tool's output will be made interpretable to end-users (clinicians, patients, participants, etc.), including how results will be explained
The protocol describes how researchers will be informed about model behavior, outputs, and limitations
The protocol describes how clinicians will be trained to interpret AI outputs
The protocol describes how end-users (e.g., participants, students, clinicians) are trained to interpret AI recommendations and when to override them
